title: fix: route user-tag taps to the group member screen for members
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/3bc2fd2a26b31776a66740df4df014b23b1e1319feacd49e667f722f9a4e3f1d.png)

Closes #681.

Tapping an @-mention inside a chat bubble used to open the start-chat shade, even when the tagged marmot was already in the group. Now the bubble checks the group roster and routes to the group member shade for members, keeping the start-chat shade for non-members and DMs.

Since the chat screen already loads the member list once via `useGroupMembers`, the bubble gets a memoized `Set<String>` instead of fetching members per bubble. That keeps the "don't fetch in every chat bubble" line from the issue satisfied.

For consistency, the start-chat shade now anchors to the top of the screen, matching the group member shade. Both shades slide in from the same spot.

title: feat(blocked-users): complete block/unblock UX
body: ## Description Completes the block/unblock feature with the two missing pieces: 1. **Hide the chat composer when the peer is blocked.** The "You blocked this user" banner already rendered in chats; only the input gate was missing. 2. **Settings → Privacy & Security → Blocked users.** A list of all blocked accounts, tap a row to open a profile-detail modal with an Unblock action. The detail opens over a blurred list following the existing `chat_info_screen` pattern (`opaque: false` + `WnOverlay(light)`). Reuses existing hooks (`useBlockActions`, `useBlockedPubkeys`, `useUserMetadata`, `useRouteRefresh`) and shared widgets (`WnSlate`, `WnOverlay`, `WnChatInfoProfileCard`, `WnUserItem`). title: Support Android in integration tests
body: ![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/dd1ac80777d20141b7bd33d3f22d917f040b45872cfbc5ca53d126f3f81f30ba.jpg) `just int-test` now runs on Android. ## What changed - `_resolve-device` falls back to `adb devices` when no booted iOS simulator is found, and skips `xcrun` on hosts where it isn't installed (so Linux works too). - `int-test` auto-injects public Nostr relays through `--dart-define=WHITENOISE_INTEGRATION_RELAYS=...` when the resolved device is an Android one. The emulator can't reach the host's localhost, so the local docker relays aren't usable there. - `integration_test/_support/app_setup.dart` reads the relay list from that dart-define (default: the same two localhost relays as before), and the TCP precheck now no-ops for non-localhost URLs. The iOS path is unchanged, and either platform can override the relay list with `WHITENOISE_INTEGRATION_RELAYS=...`. ## Why The marmot colony hibernates near the host, but our Android sibling lives one virtual network away (it can't hear the local relays burrowing at `127.0.0.1`). So when the Android marmot wants to chat, we point it at the public relays already used in production: `nos.lol`, `relay.primal.net`, `relay.damus.io`. ## How to use ```bash # iOS simulator (unchanged) just int-test # Android emulator (auto-detected, auto-uses public relays) just int-test # Override relays on any platform WHITENOISE_INTEGRATION_RELAYS=wss://my.relay just int-test ``` --- ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Tests** * Integration tests now support configurable relay URLs via environment variable * Device detection expanded to include both iOS simulators and connected Android devices * Local relay connectivity checks enhanced to work with any configured relay URL [![Review Change Stack](https://storage.googleapis.com/coderabbit_public_assets/review-stack-in-coderabbit-ui.svg)](https://app.coderabbit.ai/change-stack/marmot-protocol/whitenoise/pull/690?utm_source=github_walkthrough&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=change_stack)

title: Share media and messages via long-press chooser
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/964f746c03c694b2af67bbda86f94699187fa4934e7ac5f32e270ecde3b85138.jpg)

Long-press on media in the media modal now opens a small chooser with Save to gallery and Share. Before this, long-press would silently dump the file to the gallery with no feedback.

The message hold menu gains the same two rows: Share sends the message text and any cached attachments through the OS share sheet; Save to gallery shows up when the message has downloaded media.

Layout fixes in the hold menu preview:

- Short messages now size the preview to their natural bubble height instead of claiming the full slot.
- Media-only messages clip the timestamp row cleanly with UnconstrainedBox plus Clip.hardEdge instead of throwing a RenderFlex overflow assertion.

Marmots can now pass acorns to other marmots without losing them in the burrow.

Closes #631.

body: The group info screen should have an 'add member' button to invite new members to the group directly from group settings.

title: User tag navigation
body:
# Context
When clicking in a user tag in a message bubble, it shows the start chat screen. This is a bit unexpected comparing with other chat apps (like whatsapp or signal) where tags navigate to the same screen that you woudl see when clicking on a group member from the members lists screen.The reason for doing this is that tags in messages may tag users that are not in the group. 

# Solution
A solution that we discussed here https://github.com/marmot-protocol/whitenoise/pull/665#discussion_r3261928955 would be to keep the start chat navigation only for users that are not members of the group and for group members navigate to the group member screen

⚠️ We don't want to fetch group members in every chat bubble

title: Add 'Add members' button to group info
body:
![marmot](https://blossom.primal.net/2b00131e067d6f0b7f396f0ba20f3b74c0f07d04733e35fb36313db9f463701f.png)

## What

Admins can now add new members directly from the group info screen. Tap the new **Add members** button to open a picker, select followed users, and submit. The picker hides anyone who is already in the group.

## How

- New screen `add_group_members_screen.dart` reuses the `useUserSearch` and `useUserSelection` hooks from the new-group flow.
- New route `addGroupMembers` plus a `Routes.pushToAddGroupMembers` helper.
- Group info gets an admin-only button below **Edit group** that passes the current member list so the picker can filter them out.
- Submit calls `groups_api.addMembersToGroup` and pops back on success. Failures show an error notice and keep the user on the screen.

## Tests

- 8 widget tests for the new screen: header, candidate list, member filtering, button enable state, submit success, error notice, back navigation.
- 3 new tests in `group_info_screen_test.dart`: admin gating and navigation.
- `just precommit` passes.

A friendly marmot greets fellow marmots at the burrow door. That is the whole feature.
